column1: # Shiren GB — THE OPENING CINEMATIC, for review. `loc <TAB> english`, same shape as
# `script/prose_draft.tsv`, so it feeds the same review-then-edit loop you use everywhere
# else. Nothing here is inserted yet.
# WHY IT IS A SEPARATE FILE AND NOT `en.tsv` YET. Every `loc` in `en.tsv` is a key into
# `script/script.json`, and none of these are in `script.json` — the cinematic uses a
# different character table (`13:$7FAA`, see FINDINGS.md) and the extractor has never been
# able to read it. Merging these into `en.tsv` means teaching `extract.py` the second
# table first, so that `lint_en`, `--check` and `build.py` can all see them. That is
# session 11's engineering. **This file is the text, so the wording can be settled while
# that happens** — edit it exactly as you would `prose_draft.tsv`.
# THE GEOMETRY IS NOT YET MEASURED, so treat the widths below as provisional. What IS
# measured: the screen draws these two tilemap rows at a time (a text row plus a row of
# dakuten above it), and the Japanese lines run to about 19 characters. The English
# alphabet needs a table patch before any of this can be inserted at all — the cinematic
# table reaches font codes $0B-$38, which is `A`-`Z` and `a`-`t`, so THERE IS NO
# u, v, w, x, y AND NO `.` OR `-` until five of its 17 dead katakana slots are repointed.
# HOW THE JAPANESE WAS READ, since it is worth being able to check the work: combining
# marks PRECEDE their kana here (`むら ゙ ひと` is むらびと), the opposite of the main script;
# `$4D` takes one argument byte and `$4E` takes two, measured by drawing the line on the
# real screen and reconciling it against the bytes, not inferred from the pattern.
# `python3 tools/introtext.py build/_base_expanded.gb` dumps the program.
# WHAT I AM NOT SURE OF, and you will know better than I do: the program is ONE run of
# seven scenes, and it reads like two halves. Scenes 1-4 are the sacrifice backstory.
# Scenes 5-7 are Shiren and Koppa out on the road, past the village, talking about Keyaki
# in the past tense. Whether that second half is the opening's framing or the ENDING
# replayed in the attract loop, I cannot tell from the bytes — but either way it is in
# these same 830 bytes, so it is not a separate thing still to be found.
# ---- scene 1-3: the mother, the villager, the mother again ----
# ははおや「わたしのこが・・・」
# むらびと「かわいそうだが シキタリだ。 あきらめるしかねえ・・・」
# シキタリ is written in katakana for weight -- 仕来り, the custom. Kept as a set phrase.

column2: Villager: A pity, but it is the custom. There is nothing for it but to give her up...
